### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **9** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mention-recipient-gate.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mention-recipient-gate.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **83** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `421433d7e25f84b317047a1e0cb94928382a71b7` — the merge of head `f66324e9bc7c798670e8f56a5c269c44109b632d` into base `67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 421433d7e25f84b317047a1e0cb94928382a71b7 && git checkout 421433d7e25f84b317047a1e0cb94928382a71b7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94 f66324e9bc7c798670e8f56a5c269c44109b632d && git checkout -B drift-repro 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94 && git merge --no-ff f66324e9bc7c798670e8f56a5c269c44109b632d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 67c49d778dcc167aee0408e7cc5937cbcb46ee94` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat adopts the record below, rendered on this head by an isolated reviewer at the contract-review tier. Its mechanism notes are held by the seat. A patch round is ordered for M1, M2, M3, S1 and S2; the fix moves the head and owes a delta review. Recorded 2026-11-12T03:26Z.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9b06cd188c27d0af74c8483aadb1050744c7cad7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0093-tenancy-mode-and-membership-lifecycle.md, docs/adr/0105-group-tenancy-posture-and-first-class-org-scope.md, docs/adr/0123-no-active-organization-session-semantics.md + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-write-tenant-wall.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-operation-principals.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx, .changeset/membership-required-every-posture.md, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__core__src__security__resolve-authz-context.ts.json, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__core__src__security__tenant-layer0-verdict.ts.json

Inputs read: ruling of record 6796108313 (the one later comment on #32004 citing it, 6807809967, is a seat hand-over and changes nothing in the rule); PR #32524 body, file list (68 files) and net diff against `main`; check-runs on the head. Remainder of the diff (tests, fixtures, comment-only edits in runtime / plugin-approvals / plugin-audit / service-storage, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on the head, as read: success — Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates and every `Lint ·` leg (ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, CI/release/engine gates, the three scoped legs), Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate; its shard matrix is skipped on this event). In progress, no verdict yet — Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI. Skipped — Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Lint UI, the opt-in legs. The real-stack rule suite's 15/15 is the dev's local reading; no check-run on this head has run it yet.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `vetOrganizationClaim` reads no posture; a session's or a key's organization claim stands only on a current membership, under every posture and with none supplied — **right**, the ruling's rule exactly. Third parameter kept, optional, ignored: source-compatible; **right**.
2. A stamped API key whose owner holds no current membership in the key's organization is refused under every posture — **right** (ADR-0090 D10's 2026-09-16 note: a person's key is that person's credential; the ruling's subject is the person).
3. The org-less key's `organization_required` refusal stays `isolated`-only — **right**: it is not the membership rule; an org-less key's owner is still judged by Layer 0 under `single` and `group`.
4. Layer 0 under `single`: a person with no current membership in any organization is denied the tenant rows; everyone else keeps `none` — **right in direction, narrower than the ruling in four places**: (a) M1, (b) M2, (c) S2, (d) the platform-operator carve-out (③). Each is named below.
5. "A current membership" under `single` means any current membership, not one in the row's organization — **right as recorded** (ADR-0105 D1 stands: no wall between organizations under `single`; the amendment note says "in any organization" in terms). See ③(b).
6. System contexts, anonymous guests and non-tenant objects keep their rule — **right**; census row 6d and its site register agree with the predicate's `isSystem` read.
7. New public surface: `isOutsideEveryOrganization` (export of `@objectstack/core`) and optional `TenantLayer0Input.outsideEveryOrganization` — additive, optional, default inert; **right**. No schema key, no `packages/spec` change: `Metadata-protocol: none` is **right**.
8. Explain / delegated readers call the one spelling (`vetOrganizationClaim`) and still pass the dead argument — **right**, no second spelling introduced.
9. Match to the ruling: **not exact — narrower** (M1, M2), and the migration note the ruling requires does not hold against the tree (M3). No place found where the change is wider than the ruling.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `membership-required-every-posture.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`; BREAKING banner; migration note; one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason; both declaration lines present and identical to the PR body. This is AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 as written (a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition), and the three packages are the three whose shipped code moves; the other touched packages change comments or tests only. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check:adr-0087-registration`) are green on the head, so the disposition is registered as the gate reads it. The disposition category fits: nothing an author writes changes shape and the body carries no FROM/TO block.

Clause-②: `yes (narrowing)` — correct arm (data access narrows; BREAKING), stated once in each place; the additive export rides the same line, which the closed pair allows.

Flag for the Tier H approver, not a finding: the ruling of record says "a major, BREAKING change"; the changeset level is `patch` under AGENTS.md's level rule. If "major" was meant as the release level and not the class, the changeset must say so — the maintainer's to confirm at approval.

M3 below is also a ② matter: the migration note's "need no action" sentence is not true of the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

- (a) Contexts carrying no `accessible_org_ids` are not judged — **not acceptable as left: M2.** The dev's note describes them as hand-built in-process contexts; read against the tree, the class is wider than that. A private note is with the seat.
- (b) Under `single`, a member of one organization is not walled from another organization's rows — **answered: the ruling does not require more.** The ruling did not amend ADR-0105 D1; under `single` the deployment is one logical tenant, `organization/create` is refused, and an unbacked claim is dropped before Layer 0. One residue to **escalate** to the maintainer for an explicit yes: a `single` deployment that holds more than one organization (a degraded boot under `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY=1`, or legacy rows) admits a member of any of them to all of them. The amendment note states "in any organization" plainly, so this is on the record, not hidden.
- (c) Intermediate commits — **squash-merge required.** `8a85882ca` is a `wip:` commit, and commits before `e2f549242` carried comments and a migration note phrased as before/after; `e2f549242` rewrote them to the rule. What they said restates ADR-0093 D8.1 as already published, so nothing mechanism-level is exposed, but only a squash keeps `main`'s history at the wording of the head.
- Platform operator — **escalate.** The predicate excepts the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung on every tenant object under `single`; the walled postures except it only on posture-permitting objects, so the amendment's phrase "the answers `isolated` and `group` give the same person" is not true of this person. It is pre-existing reach, kept, and the amendment note records it; the ruling's text makes no operator exception, so the maintainer should accept it by name at approval.
- A composition with no SecurityPlugin does not enforce the rule (the engine's own verdict projects only a driver scope, and a `deny` with no active organization projects none) — same as every other authorization rule and as `isolated` answers there; noted, no action.
- Public text at the head — PR title and body, changeset, ADR notes, docs, test names, code comments — stays at rule level. No sentence found that describes the earlier behaviour as an attack or gives a reproduction. The struck-through D8.1 and the replaced docs callout necessarily show the old published non-goal.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0093` (hit).** The amendment note is in the right place (status line, D8 summary, D8.1 struck, Deferred line) and states the rule as ruled. Against its first consumer and execution plan:

- **M3 · must-fix — the "Consequences" paragraph and the changeset's migration note do not hold against the tree.** The note says D6 "and its `app:seeded` re-run are how a single-org deployment's people get the membership that admits them", and the changeset says such deployments "need no action: every user is bound … when they are created and when seed data settles". In the tree the backfill is one-time per deployment (`membership-backfill-ledger.ts`, recorded in `sys_migration`); `auth-plugin.ts` says of the `app:seeded` trigger "the ledger makes it a no-op once the one-time pass has been recorded"; the creation-time bind is best-effort (a failure warns and the user is created without a membership); a per-user backfill bind failure is skipped; with no readable ledger the pass does not run; and users created while the policy was `invite-only` are deliberately never swept. Until this PR none of that cost anything. After it, each of those people is refused all tenant data on a deployment that kept every default. D6's own text ("seeded users depend on this backfill as their only net") is the plan the amendment leans on, and it no longer describes the code. Required: the amendment and the migration note state who can be member-less on a default deployment and what the operator does (how to find them, `add-member`), or the code restores a net; "need no action" goes.
- **S1 · should-fix — D1's rejected alternative is left standing against the amendment.** D1 keeps `invite-only` because "a shared service with app end-users who are deliberately not teammates" is legitimate, and `tenancy-modes.mdx`'s policy table still recommends `invite-only` for exactly that deployment. Under the amended rule those end-users reach no tenant data. The note should say what that deployment does now (a membership of the fitting grade, e.g. the `external` role) and the table row should stop reading as a recommendation.

**`docs/adr/0105` (hit).** Both inline notes agree with the verdict function. nit: the D1 table cell now reads "none between organizations (Layer 0 inert); a person outside every organization is denied" — "inert" and "denied" in one cell; say "inert between organizations".

**`docs/adr/0123` (hit).** The inline note is accurate for the caller's own writes and for reads. It is **not yet true of every delegated write — M1.**

**`core/…/resolve-authz-context.ts`.** Agrees with the contract sentence by sentence: both arms call the one check with no posture; the dropped claim re-resolves with no organization; membership is read from `sys_member` on each resolution with ADR-0091 windows; the grants cache that could span requests is off by default and was not touched. The anchor JSON's invariant matches. No finding.

**`core/…/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts`.**
- **M2 · must-fix — the predicate's "no set, not judged" rule leaves the ruling unenforced for person contexts the platform itself builds.** Under `group` an absent set denies and under `isolated` a missing organization denies; `single` is now the one posture where an absent set admits. The docblock justifies it as "was not built by the resolver and states nothing about membership"; read against the live tree, that is not a sufficient description of the person contexts the platform builds outside the request resolver. The rule "under every posture … judged on each request" must hold for them too: either they carry the resolver's set, or the `single` branch fails toward the wall for a person context without one; and the predicate's docblock and the ADR sentence "the one predicate every reader asks" are corrected to what is true. A private note is with the seat.
- **S2 · should-fix — the `single` branch's "outside tenancy" set is wider than the walled postures'.** The walled ladder's rungs are not all asked on the `single` branch, so the amendment's claim of the same answers as `isolated` and `group` is not true for one object class. A private note is with the seat.
- nit: `TenantLayer0Input.outsideEveryOrganization` says "only `single` reads this field" — true; say also that a caller must not set it from anything but the predicate.

**`plugin-security/…/security-plugin-write-tenant-wall.ts`.**
- **M1 · must-fix — the delegation half of the rule is not held on every write path under `single`.** `organizationWallRefusal`'s own comment ("an on-behalf-of write may not land a row the delegator itself could not place"), the amendment's Delegation bullet and the changeset's delegation line state a rule the function's `single` arm does not ask of the delegator in every case, and `delegated-organization-membership.test.ts` pins `single` in one of the two context shapes the walled postures are pinned in. Read, not probed. A private note is with the seat.
- nit: the refusal's developer message says "tenancy posture 'single' walls 'OBJECT'" for a `single` refusal; under `single` the sentence should name the membership rule.

**`plugin-security/…/tenant-layer.ts`.** One builder, one predicate read, comments agree. No finding beyond S2, which lives in the verdict.

**`plugin-security/…/security-plugin-operation-principals.ts`, `explain-engine.ts`, `security-plugin-explain-access.ts`.** Comment and message edits only; they agree with the check as it now is. See M1 for the one place the delegation rule is not yet whole.

**`objectql/…/engine-driver-options.ts`.** Reads the same predicate off the same context; agrees. nit: the comment "so the engine's verdict is the wall's" should not be read as enforcement — under `single` a `deny` projects no driver scope.

**`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`.** Row 6d and the register line agree with the predicate. No finding.

**`content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`.** The callout states the rule. Carries S1 (policy table) and M3 (the backfill paragraph still reads as a standing net).

**Design attempts, by reading:** API key stamped / org-less, under each posture — holds. Membership removed mid-session — holds on the next request (no cross-request cache by default). Invite-only and backfill off — rule holds; documentation does not (M3, S1). OAuth-delegated agent — holds (the established session is the user's, so the set is the user's). Delegation under `single` — M1. Person contexts without a set — M2. System contexts — unchanged. Platform operator — ③.

Must-fix: M1, M2, M3. Should-fix: S1, S2. Nits: four, listed in place.
